segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
I signed the twins as visitors because Sera made me.

MIRA.

TOMAS.

They were delighted.

I was not.

Later that afternoon Tomas told my father, "Dada has to write name."

My father asked why.

Tomas said, "Sera boss."

My father laughed for an unreasonable amount of time.

Family is support until evidence emerges.

Months later East Four had a real problem.

Market branch regulator fault.

Not dangerous yet.

Could become dangerous if left.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Sera called district for inspection because the failure pattern touched old support geometry.

She called me.

Not Dera.

Not because she liked me.

Because the job fit.

I arrived.

Signed in.

Without being told.

That mattered more than I wanted it to.

Took a gauge from the cage.

Wrote my name.

Sera saw.

Said nothing.

Cruel restraint.

We worked six hours.

Her crew owned the station.

I owned the survey question.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
At one point I wanted the branch held at fifty percent for a test.

Sera said forty.

"Why?"

"Upper bearing ran hot this morning."

"Not in the log."

"Night hand told me at shift change."

I looked at the shift sheet.

Written there.

Her new handoff system.

Forty was enough.

We tested.

Found the fault.

No argument.

At the end I returned the gauge.

Signed it in.

Sera said, "You can keep a district key to the cage if Halden approves."

I looked at her.

"Why?"

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
"You use it enough."

"Thought you liked paperwork."

"I like knowing who can open things."

Different.

I understood.

Mostly.

"Thank you."

Sera nodded.

I almost apologized for the Dera sentence.

Months late.

Still possible.

"Also, I was an ass about the chamber access."

"Yes."

"I was going to apologize."

"You did."

"That was not enough response."

"What do you want?"

"Something difficult."

"No."

I laughed.

There it was.

I did not need Sera to become Dera.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
I needed East Four to remain a station after the person who taught me it left.

That required someone new enough to change the locks.

When I got home, Tomas was drawing on scrap paper at the table.

Mira was telling Nessa a story that had begun before I entered and showed no signs of needing me.

Tomas looked up.

"You write name?"

I took off my coat.

"Yes."

"Because Sera?"

"Because it is her station."

Mira stopped talking.

Both children looked at me.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Then Tomas nodded.

"Sera boss."

"Foreman."

"Boss."

Nessa laughed.

I let him have it.

Growth.
